title: Abba Chalifa Kirvaya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Bava Batra 123a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.123a.21), he asked Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba a question. [Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 4:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.4.1.4) teaches: “Abba bar Chalifai bar Karei: When does this apply? To produce definitely liable for tithes.” Rabbi Chiyya bar Wa was in Rome and saw them redeeming produce. He said: “The one who ruled for them was Chilfari bar Kirei” (possibly a place-name). In [the old Midrash Tehillim, chapter 20](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.20.5), Rabban Gamliel (identified by Hyman as the son of Rabbi Yehudah the second Nasi) went to Abba Chalfa ben Kruyah to have him pray for him.[^1][^2]

notes.text: [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1307&lang=en) presents the Bava Batra and Maaser Sheni passages together. The Babylonian passage names Abba Chalifa Karoya; the Jerusalem Talmud gives different forms in the ruling and the incident in Rome. Its translator understands the designation as “small-town man” and distinguishes the two men.

The linked Midrash Tehillim has Rabban Gamliel go to Chalfa ben Kruyah, without Abba. It gives two versions of his blessing and does not give Gamliel’s father’s name. The possible place-name and the identification of Gamliel are Hyman’s suggestions.
